chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated, from al-Barqī, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the skins of al-sammūr, and he said: “What kind of thing is that? Is it the dark-colored one?” I said: It is the black one. He said: “Does it hunt?” I said: Yes, it catches chickens and pigeons. He said: “No.”

It is also possible that by “in” he intended according to what we have mentioned before this place. It is also possible that he intended when it is on a cap or a garment by which salat (prayer) is not complete, and whatever has come in the reports regarding the concession of wearing these things during the state of salat (prayer), the discussion concerning it is as we have mentioned.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no problem with salat (prayer) in pure khazz, but salat (prayer) in it is not permissible if it is adulterated with rabbit fur and what resembles it.

key_terms.السَّمُّورِ: sable or a fur-bearing animal whose skin is being asked about in relation to salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is under discussion
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a specific fabric or fur material discussed in legal rulings of salat (prayer)
key_terms.جُلُودِ: skins or hides used as material for garments
key_terms.مَغْشُوشًا: adulterated or mixed with another material
key_terms.وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbit fur, mentioned as an invalidating admixture for prayer garments
key_terms.يَصِيدُ: hunts; indicating the animal is predatory

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) permissible in clothing made from al-sammūr or khazz fur?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain animal furs, especially al-sammūr and pure khazz. It indicates disapproval or impermissibility regarding the fur of predatory animals, while allowing pure khazz so long as it is not mixed with rabbit fur or similar materials. The passage also preserves a juristic explanation reconciling related reports about wearing such items in prayer.
